newsitem.title: GERMANY: Polish, Czech floods could cost DM10 bln - Munich Re.
newsitem.headline: Polish, Czech floods could cost DM10 bln - Munich Re.

text.p: The catastrophic floods sweeping through central Europe could cause damage costing some 10 billion marks in Poland and the Czech Republic alone, the world's leading reinsurer Munich Re said on Monday.

The reinsurance group, which estimates its own exposure to the flooding at tens of millions of marks, said preliminary calculations suggested the total economic cost of the disaster would be three to five billion marks each in Poland and the Czech Republic, and significantly lower in Germany.
That would leave the insurance industry facing costs of up to one billion marks, assuming insurers take on some 10 percent of the costs.
Munich Re (Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG) board member Wolf Otto Bauer warned that the estimates were based on incomplete information.
"Clearly the waters have to recede. The primary insurers also need to carry out investigations which could take several weeks," Bauer told a news conference.
But he added that the flooding was "certainly not one of the largest incidents" ever to affect the insurance industry, particularly since there was miminal industrial activity in the areas affected.
The new estimates far outstrip last week's forecasts, when Munich Re placed the flooding costs in Poland and the Czech Republic at 1.5 billion marks.

The floods, among the worst this century, have claimed over 100 lives in Poland and the Czech Republic this month. Germany has escaped the worst of the floods, but damage to homes and crops has been extensive.
Bauer refused to estimate the cost of the flooding in Germany, where the Oder river in eastern Germany is at record levels, leaving thousands preparing for evacuation.
However he said the cost would be significantly below levels in other countries, as the affected area had a low population density as well as being predominantly agricultural.
